idea: Take profit earlier on FADE: full exit or partial at +0.5R to +1.5R, higher-low trail, reversal-bar exit, bigger locks (governor question after the 10-28 SOXS trade)

result: Every variant lost to the live rules: full exit at +1R PF 1.96 +21.5%, at +1.5R PF 2.80 +40.5%; sell 1/3 at +0.75R PF 3.57 +54.1%; higher-low trail from +1R PF 2.88 +42.7%; reversal-bar exit from +0.5R PF 4.04 +66.8%; lock +0.30R PF 4.10 +68.0%, +0.40R PF 3.35 +55.1%. The edge lives in the runners that reach 2R.

idea: Early tell for choppy FADE trades: 2 or more closes below entry in the first 30 minutes, then exit earlier (governor question)
method: tools/backtest/early_tell_rh.py, results/early_tell_rh.txt, all 90 Robinhood setups for the tell, the 63 account trades for the exits
result: The tell is real: 23 choppy trades averaged +0.14R and reached 2R 30% of the time, the other 67 averaged +1.24R and reached 2R 52%. But no exit treatment beat the base: best was sell half at +0.75R, PF 4.64 +83.9% against 4.81 +89.3%; a raised lock for them was a wash (at best PF 4.82). Now shadowed forward as ideas fade.chop.2red.*.

Walk-forward picks lost to live under all four rules (+11.9/+93.2/+16.4/+2.0 vs +140.7)
verdict: not adopted; offered as "push system 1" / "push system 2"; tuned picks do not transfer in walk-forward

idea: Rebuild systems 1-3 with TRAIN = 2022, 2024, 2026 and TEST = 2023, 2025: robust tune, most-consistent-months tune (each year alone), new systems re-chosen, parallel vs replacement

result: Live test 2023 -29.8, 2025 +18.3 (-16.9% compounded). System 1 pick -30.2, +15.9 (worse than live both years; score-to-test rank correlation +0.15). idea: Overnight leg sizing and risk: long signal or long + dip, 100/50/33/25% of cash, cost doubled, FADE at 100/50/0%
method: tools/backtest/overnight_size.py; baseline v5.2.51; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025; whole-period drawdown and A1.13 15% stop count
result: Long signal at 50%: +136.7, +36.8, +12.8, +113.0, +204.0 (average 2022-25 +74.8 vs +67.6), max DD 23.1 vs 25.4, 15% stop fires 2x vs 5x, worst night -4.1%, passes with cost doubled. Long + dip at 50%: average +84.7, 2026 below baseline, fails the test rule with cost doubled. Baseline book trips the 15% stop 5 times in the backtest
verdict: not adopted (A1.8); recommended form if the governor approves: long signal only at 50% of cash

idea: Universe check for the overnight leg: drop one of the six proxies, add one of 12 new ones
method: tools/backtest/overnight_universe.py; baseline v5.2.51 + overnight long at 50%; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: No change passes. Five qualify on train (EEM, FXI, XLRE, XOP, XLU) and none beats the baseline in both test years. The overnight leg alone is positive on 10 of 12 new proxies (+0.18 to +0.62% a leg), so the effect is general, but one position a night chosen by volume gains nothing from more funds
verdict: ADOPTED: overnight leg on the six proxies (v5.2.52), governor instruction 2026-11-14; universe unchanged

idea: Stops, targets, breakeven locks, trails and exit times for every live system, ranked by return and by win rate
method: tools/backtest/exit_all.py (900 exits for the 9:35 systems, 54 overnight, 24 FADE, 6 PULLBACK) and exit_overnight_hold.py (18 book-level hold variants); baseline v5.2.52 book; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: 0 of 930 day-trade exits pass. Best win rate uses a 0.5% target: IBS-LONG 71%, MIRROR 80%, DIP 72% (live 55/45/58%) and costs 28.8, 24.6 and 4.2 points of average yearly return. Overnight held to the next close looks better alone and fails in the book: 84% of overnight days also carry an IBS-LONG signal

idea: Tom Hougaard day-based setups: Thursday-Friday-Monday, Monday-Thursday, Monday-extreme failed breaks, gap fill, School Run, First Bar, Rule of 4 on FOMC days; also as filters on the live systems
method: tools/backtest/hougaard.py to hougaard5.py; six proxies, 3x legs, Massive tape 2022-2026; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025; alone and added to the live book; placebo and random-draw controls
result: 0 setups pass after controls. TFM: Monday breaks Friday low 54% vs 35% but as a trade PF 0.81 to 1.05. MTWT at 9:35 PF 1.38 and passed the rule, but Thursdays without the pattern earn more (+0.36% vs +0.48% a trade), the Wednesday placebo gives PF 1.41 and random Thursdays reach 94% of the setup. Gap fill PF 0.77 to 0.95, School Run 1.02, First Bar 0.99 to 1.04, Monday failed break 0.98, Rule of 4 0.59. As filters on IBS systems: fail
verdict: not adopted; the pattern frequencies are real but untradable

idea: Entry timing: later or earlier fills for the 9:35 family, fill slippage and a 5-minute delay, overnight entry earlier than 15:55, overnight exit at 9:30 to 10:00, overnight slippage
method: tools/backtest/entry_timing.py; live joint book v5.2.59 as baseline; one change at a time; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: 9:35 is the best entry bar: 9:30 -10.5 points a year, 9:40 -15.1, 9:45 -36.5, 10:05 -35.8, 10:35 -52.2. Slippage is the main risk: +0.05% worse fill costs 18.6 points a year, +0.10% costs 34.0, +0.20% costs 66.6 (average 2022-25 falls from +74.8 to +8.2). A 5-minute delay costs 15.1. Overnight entry time is not monotonic (15:45 -3.3, 15:30 +1.8, 15:00 -8.3, 14:00 -10.9, 13:00 +4.3 and passes the rule) so the 13:00 pass is noise, and 13:00 to 15:55 overlaps the day trades. Overnight exit 9:40 +2.5, 9:45 +3.3 qualify but fail 2025. Overnight slip 0.10% each way costs 14.2 points
verdict: not adopted; live entry and exit times stay. Track real fill slippage on the first 20 trades per system

idea: Direct directional re-check of the Hougaard Thursday-Friday-Monday claim (Monday falls after Friday high at or below Thursday high and a break of Friday low)
method: tools/backtest/hougaard6.py; proxy returns only; controls: other Mondays, the same structure on Tuesday to Friday, 5000 random draws
result: Open-to-close on pattern Mondays -0.20% vs +0.26% on other Mondays (347 events, t -2.1). The fall is selection: the same structure on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday falls more (-0.46%, -0.54%, -0.52%). From the break of Friday low to the close the proxy RISES +0.23% (55% up), so a short at the break loses. Gap-down Mondays rebound +0.57% (68% up). Pattern effect is -0.5% in 2022 and about 0 in 2023-2025
verdict: not adopted; the claim measures the day breaking its low, not a tradable edge

idea: Measure the live health bands (health.py) on the full five-year backtest
method: tools/backtest/health_bt.py on the 942 backtest trades; rolling 30 and 20 trade windows per system; share of windows in each band, by year, worst windows, trade frequency, percentiles
result: A system running exactly to the backtest still hits ACT (profit factor under 1.0) in 42% of 30-trade windows for FADE, 31% PULLBACK, 22% MIRROR, 16% OVERNIGHT, 10% IBS-LONG, 2% DIP. Longest runs under 1.0: PULLBACK 520 days, FADE 252, MIRROR 178, IBS-LONG 57, OVERNIGHT 51. Median 30-trade PF: FADE 1.10, PULLBACK 1.76, IBS-LONG 1.54, MIRROR 2.17, DIP 1.49, OVERNIGHT 1.27. Frequency check: 16 to 30% of windows run under 60% of pace. Candidate bands (5th percentile as ACT): PF FADE 0.47, PULLBACK 0.27, IBS-LONG 0.92, MIRROR 0.87, DIP 1.11, OVERNIGHT 0.78
verdict: no change made; bands need the governor written instruction

idea: PULLBACK exit with three tranches: 1/3 at the morning high, 1/3 at a second level above it, 1/3 runner on the 20-EMA close (governor question)
method: tools/backtest/pb_three_tranche.py; second level = high + 0.5 to 3R, entry + 3 to 6R, or high + 1 to 3% of entry; stop after sale 2 at breakeven or at the high; 24 variants plus 1/2-1/2 and 1/4-1/4-1/2; judged inside the live joint book v5.2.59; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: 0 of 24 variants pass or qualify. The live exit (1/3 at the high, 2/3 runner) averages +74.8% a year 2022-25 and every variant is lower: high + 0.5R to 3R -6.4 to -3.6 points, entry + 3R to 6R -4.6 to -2.1, high + 1 to 3% -6.0 to -4.8. 1/2 at the high with a 1/2 runner -3.5, 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/2 -3.0. The second level is reached on 18% of trades (high + 1R). The PULLBACK edge is in the runner: selling more of it early lowers PF from 1.21 to 1.09 to 1.20

idea: PULLBACK runner fade-sell rules after UVXY peaked 23.24 and the runner gave it back to breakeven (governor question)
method: tools/backtest/pb_fade_exit.py; give back f of the open gain once m R up; close p % under the best close; stop lock at +nR once mR up; 9-EMA and 3-bar-low runners; 22 rules inside the live joint book v5.2.60; train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: 0 of 22 pass. Best: give back 40% once 3R up, +0.2 points a year (qualifies on train, loses 2025). Tight rules cost the most: give back 30% at 1R -6.6, close 1% under the best -7.3, 9-EMA runner -3.7. Wide rules almost never fire (+0.0). On 2026-11-17 the 40%-after-3R rule would have sold the UVXY runner at about 22.29 (+$59) instead of breakeven
verdict: not adopted by the rule; neutral option offered to the governor

idea: Sell more of PULLBACK at the morning high, or cash out the runner at a fixed gain (governor question after a +4.4% day ended flat)
method: tools/backtest/pb_cashout.py; share at the high 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, all; runner limit at +2 to +6%; 1/2 at the high + runner limit; live joint book; five years
result: Every step toward cashing out lowers return. Sell at the high: 1/2 -3.5, 2/3 -6.9, all -13.7 points a year (PF 1.21 -> 1.04). Runner cashed at +2% to +6%: -12.7 to -5.1. 1/2 at the high plus a runner limit: -9.3 to -7.0. The PULLBACK edge comes from the few runners that keep going; selling everything at the high leaves almost no edge (PF 1.04)
verdict: not adopted; live exit (1/3 at the high, runner, 3R giveback from 11-18) stays

idea: Signals for more or less runner room, early loss cuts, and an audit of the v5.2.61 3R giveback (governor question)
method: tools/backtest/pb_signals.py; base = live v5.2.61; VWAP, 9-EMA after 12:00, 9-EMA on 1.5x volume, ignore the 20-EMA while above VWAP, two closes under the 20-EMA; loss cuts before the 1/3 (no +0.5R after 30/60 min, -0.5R close after 15 min, close under VWAP); live joint book, train 2022/2024/2026, test 2023/2025
result: 3R giveback fires on 9 of 444 trades (2%): helped 4, hurt 4, -1.2% of position in total, +0.2 points a year in the book (neutral). 0 of 9 signals pass. Less room: VWAP 0.0, 9-EMA after 12:00 -2.1, 9-EMA on volume -3.4. More room: above VWAP +0.3, two closes -0.3. Loss cuts: no +0.5R after 30 min +1.4 and -0.5R after 15 min +1.6 but both lose 2024 and 2026 (fail train); 60 min -0.2; VWAP -1.0
verdict: not adopted; giveback kept as neutral at the governor choice

idea: Lock the PULLBACK runner stop at the morning high (or halfway) once price clears the high by x R (governor: gain cuts past the high)
method: tools/backtest/pb_lock_high.py; base live v5.2.61; x = 0, 0.5, 1, 2 R; live joint book; train/test rule
result: 0 of 8 pass, all below or equal to live: stop to the high -2.5 to -0.7 points a year, stop halfway -2.3 to 0.0. Earlier the same day: second sale at high + 0.5R to 3R or high + 1 to 3% -6.4 to -3.6, runner limit at +2 to +6% -12.7 to -5.1

idea: When the 1/3 fills at the morning high, move the runner stop 1/4 of the way from breakeven to the high instead of breakeven (governor question)
method: pb_lock_high.manage with lvl 0.10 and 0.25, trigger at the high, 0.5R and 1R past it; live joint book; train/test rule
result: Stop 25% of the way at the high: -2.3 points a year (PF 1.21 -> 1.16); 10% of the way: -3.6. Delayed to 0.5R past the high: -2.5 both. Delayed to 1R past the high: 0.0 (qualifies on train, fails test). Runners often dip back to just above breakeven before running, so any stop above breakeven at the fill gets hit on the trades that pay

idea: Giveback gaps in FADE, IBS-LONG, MIRROR, DIP (governor: other systems, before I lose out on a $60 gain)
method: tools/backtest/giveback_all.py; round trips (reached 1/2/3R, ended under +0.2R); giveback once m R up (1 to 3), f 40/50%; live joint book v5.2.61; train/test rule
result: Round trips from 2R: FADE 0 of 53, IBS-LONG 1 of 27, MIRROR 2 of 32, DIP 0 of 19; from 3R: 0 in every system (FADE already has the +0.15R lock, the 2R third and a 2-ATR chandelier; the 9:35 family exits at 15:55). Givebacks: FADE best 40% at 2R +0.3 (qual, fails test); 9:35 family 40% at 2R +1.5 (qual, loses 2023), 40% at 3R +1.8 but only from 2025 (train years unchanged), 1R versions -24 to -28. 0 pass. OVERNIGHT has no intraday hold
verdict: not adopted; the gap existed only in the PULLBACK runner, now covered by v5.2.61
